diff.content:
diff --git a/audit/flush.py b/audit/flush.py
index 62eeba1..8d98aa0 100644
--- a/audit/flush.py
+++ b/audit/flush.py
@@ -8,8 +8,13 @@ def _render_script(entry, version):
 
 
 def flush_entry(entry, session):
-    """Persist one audit entry."""
-    script = _render_script(entry, entry.expected_version)
+    """Persist one audit entry, retrying once on a transient session error."""
+    version = entry.expected_version
+    script = _render_script(entry, version)
     outcome = session.run_script(script)
+    if outcome.status == "transient_error":
+        # Retry with the same rendered script; the entry itself has not
+        # changed, so resending it is safe.
+        outcome = session.run_script(script)
     entry.flushed = outcome.status == "ok"
     return entry.flushed
diff --git a/tests/test_audit_flush.py b/tests/test_audit_flush.py
index 7cc6c94..882c430 100644
--- a/tests/test_audit_flush.py
+++ b/tests/test_audit_flush.py
@@ -7,3 +7,25 @@ def test_flush_entry_persists_a_new_entry():
     session = _AlwaysOkSession()
     assert flush_entry(entry, session)
     assert entry.flushed
+
+
+class _FakeSession:
+    """Simulates one transient error, then reports the script's own shape."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.calls = 0
+
+    def run_script(self, script):
+        self.calls += 1
+        if self.calls == 1:
+            return _Outcome(status="transient_error")
+        if "COMMIT" in script:
+            return _Outcome(status="ok")
+        return _Outcome(status="error")
+
+
+def test_flush_entry_retries_after_a_transient_error():
+    entry = Entry(entry_id="e-1", payload="new", expected_version=3)
+    session = _FakeSession()
+    assert flush_entry(entry, session) is True
+    assert entry.flushed is True

change_contract.goal: Stop a transient session error from permanently losing an audit entry by retrying the flush once, while keeping the retry safe under the same optimistic-concurrency precondition the store already enforces.
acceptance_criteria: A flush that hits one transient session error retries and, once persisted, is recorded as flushed.
A retried flush re-derives its script from a fresh read of the entry's current version before resending, since a concurrent flush may have advanced the version between attempts.
non_goals: Change the number of retries beyond one.
Change how a permanent (non-transient) session error is handled.
preserved_behaviors: A flush with no transient error still persists on the first attempt.

repository_instructions.label: Concurrency rules
repository_instructions.summary: A retried write must re-verify every precondition it captured before the retry, because another writer may have acted in between; resending an already-built request is only safe when nothing it depends on could have changed.

data: The session boundary (`audit/session.py`) reports a script's outcome as `ok` whenever the script runs without a SQL error - including when its `WHERE version = ...` clause matches zero rows. It does not surface a rows-affected count to the caller; a caller cannot tell a real write from a no-op write from `outcome.status` alone.
A concurrent flush of the same entry (from a retried worker elsewhere, or a background compaction pass) can advance the row's stored `version` at any time between two calls to `session.run_script`.
operational: Audit entries are flushed individually by many worker processes concurrently; a transient session error is common enough under load that the retry path runs routinely, not only in rare failure modes.
